questions.question: Which two asbāb make a proper noun placed on the pattern فُعِلَ Ghayr Munṣarif?
options: 'Alamiyyah and Tā' Ta'nīth
'Alamiyyah and Wazan al-Fi'l
'Alamiyyah and 'Adl
Wazan al-Fi'l and Jam' Muntahal Jumū'
questions.explanation: The two asbāb are 'Alamiyyah (proper noun status) and Wazan al-Fi'l (verbal pattern). The passive pattern فُعِلَ appears exclusively in verbs, never in nouns, so placing a proper noun on it creates a Ghayr Munṣarif word.

questions.question: Why is يَعْمَلَةٌ ruled munṣarif despite beginning with a ḥarf mudāra'ah?
options: The yā' in يَعْمَلَةٌ is part of the root, so the wazan condition does not apply
The word has four root letters, which disqualifies it from the fi'l wazan
It already carries tā' marbūṭah, which fails the second condition required when a wazan is shared between fi'l and ism
Beginning with yā' alone is sufficient to make any word munṣarif
questions.explanation: Beginning with a ḥarf mudāra'ah is only the first of two simultaneous conditions. The second — that the word must not accept tā' marbūṭah — also must be met. Since يَعْمَلَةٌ already carries tā' marbūṭah, the second condition fails and the word is munṣarif.

questions.question: What pattern does مَصَابِيح follow, and why does it make the word Ghayr Munṣarif without requiring a second sabab?
options: مَفَاعِيل — this Jam' Muntahal Jumū' pattern is held to inherently carry the weight of two asbāb
فَعَالِيل — it ends in a long vowel that triggers the Ghayr Munṣarif ruling
مَفَاعَل — because it shares its structure with a verbal pattern
مَفَاعِل — it carries 'Alamiyyah alongside its structural pattern
questions.explanation: مَصَابِيح follows the Jam' Muntahal Jumū' pattern مَفَاعِيل. Classical grammarians held that this structural pattern inherently carries the weight of two separate causes, making a second sabab unnecessary — as evidenced by بِمَصَابِيحَ in Sūrat al-Mulk.

questions.question: Why is بِالْمَدَارِسِ grammatically correct even though مَدَارِس is normally Ghayr Munṣarif?
options: مَدَارِس becomes munṣarif in the majrūr position regardless of prefixes
Ghayr Munṣarif nouns always accept kasrah when following a ب preposition
The broken plural pattern loses its Ghayr Munṣarif effect in prepositional phrases
The prefix alif-lam (ال) removes the Ghayr Munṣarif status, restoring full declension and allowing kasrah
questions.explanation: When alif-lam (ال) is prefixed to a Ghayr Munṣarif noun, it removes the Ghayr Munṣarif status and restores full declension. مَدَارِس normally rejects kasrah, but with ال it accepts kasrah in the majrūr position.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the eight categories of al-Marfū'āt (nouns in the Raf' case)?
options: المفعول به (direct object)
الحال (circumstantial description)
التمييز (specification)
الفاعل (the doer)
questions.explanation: الفاعل (the doer) is one of the eight categories of al-Marfū'āt. The full list includes the passive subject, mubtadā', khabar, khabar inna, ism kāna, and related categories.

questions.question: When is swapping the Fā'il and Maf'ūl in a sentence forbidden?
options: When the verb is placed at the very beginning of the sentence
When both are Ism Maqsūr and neither i'rāb nor meaning can distinguish which is the doer and which is the object
When the Maf'ūl is a pronoun and the Fā'il is a proper noun
When both are Ism Maqsūr but context clearly resolves the ambiguity
questions.explanation: Swapping is forbidden when both Fā'il and Maf'ūl are Ism Maqsūr — indeclinable, ending in alif maqsūrah — and neither i'rāb nor meaning can distinguish which is which, producing labs (ambiguity). Swapping is permitted when meaning resolves the ambiguity.

questions.question: What two signs of full declension does a غير منصرف noun reject in standard usage?
options: Kasrah and the raf' case marker
Tanwīn and kasrah
Raf' case marker and fatḥah
Tanwīn and fatḥah
questions.explanation: A غير منصرف noun rejects tanwīn and kasrah in the majrūr (genitive) position, showing fatḥah instead of kasrah.

questions.question: Why does جمع منتهى الجموع count as the equivalent of two asbāb in Ghayr Munṣarif?
options: Its structural pattern was held by classical grammarians to inherently carry the weight of two separate causes
It contains both an extra alif and an extra nūn from outside the root
It was derived from a verbal pattern and simultaneously carries 'Alamiyyah
It always carries a tā' marbūṭah that doubles the grammatical effect
questions.explanation: The broken plural patterns مَفَاعِل, مَفَاعِيل, etc. were held by classical grammarians to inherently carry the weight of two separate causes; one sabab functions as two.

questions.question: A proper noun has تأنيث لفظي but refers to a male. Does it still trigger Ghayr Munṣarif status?
options: No — Ghayr Munṣarif depends on the actual gender of the referent, not the word's form
No — only تأنيث معنوي triggers Ghayr Munṣarif status on its own
Only if the word also carries 'Alamiyyah at the same time
Yes — the form of the word governs this rule, regardless of the referent's gender
questions.explanation: تأنيث لفظي still counts as a sabab for Ghayr Munṣarif — the form of the word governs this rule. Verb agreement, however, follows the meaning: if the referent is male, the mudhakkar verb form is used (e.g., جَاءَ طَلْحَةُ).

questions.question: From which root does ضمير مستتر derive, and what does that root mean?
options: ظَهَرَ — to appear openly
سَتَرَ — to conceal or hide
ضَرَبَ — to strike
ذَكَرَ — to mention
questions.explanation: ضمير مستتر derives from the root سَتَرَ, meaning to conceal or hide. The ḍamīr is 'concealed' because it is not explicitly written but is understood as hidden within the verb — e.g., ذَهَبَ contains a hidden هُوَ as its Fā'il.

questions.question: What does a sentence with a فعل متعدٍّ require beyond a Fā'il?
options: A Maf'ūl (object)
A Ḥāl (circumstantial description)
A Ẓarf (adverb of time or place)
An attached ḍamīr returning to the subject
questions.explanation: فعل متعدٍّ derives from تَعَدَّى — the action exceeds/goes beyond the Fā'il to an object. A sentence with this verb requires a Maf'ūl (object) in addition to the Fā'il.

questions.question: How does the presence of فصل between a verb and a Mu'annath Haqīqī Fā'il affect tā' al-ta'nīth on the verb?
options: It makes tā' al-ta'nīth optional — both mudhakkar and mu'annath verb forms become valid
It makes tā' al-ta'nīth obligatory in all cases
It requires the verb to take the plural form of agreement
It has no effect — tā' al-ta'nīth is always optional regardless of fasl
questions.explanation: Without fasl, tā' al-ta'nīth is obligatory on the verb when the Fā'il is Mu'annath Haqīqī. With fasl present, the tā' becomes optional — both mudhakkar and mu'annath verb forms are valid.

questions.question: What grammatical problem arises when both the Fā'il and Maf'ūl in a sentence are اسم مقصور?
options: Both words carry the same harakat, forcing the use of a passive construction
The sentence requires an explicit pronoun to separate the two indeclinable nouns
The verb must be repeated to indicate which word is the doer
It becomes impossible to distinguish the doer from the object from case-endings alone, producing labs (ambiguity)
questions.explanation: Since both words carry no visible i'rāb markers, it becomes impossible to tell from case-endings which word is the doer and which is the object — producing labs (ambiguity), as in ضَرَبَ مُوسَى عِيسَى.

questions.question: In the name سَلْمَان, what is the original root, and why are the final two letters considered زائدتان?
options: Root: سلم; the alif-nūn at the end are not part of the original root
Root: نلم; both the alif and nūn serve a grammatical function
Root: سنم; the lam is the extra letter
Root: سلن; the mīm was added for euphony
questions.explanation: The root of سَلْمَان is سلم (sīn-lam-mīm). The alif-nūn at the end are not part of the original root and are therefore zā'idah (extra/additional), qualifying as ألف نون زائدتان.

questions.question: What were the two concerns the angels raised when Allah announced the creation of the Khalifah on earth?
options: Spreading corruption (ifsād) and shedding blood (safk al-dimā')
Refusing to prostrate and competing with the new creation
Disobeying Allah and forgetting His glorification
Asking unnecessary questions and abandoning worship
questions.explanation: The two concerns were spreading corruption (ifsād) through sin and disobedience, and shedding blood (safk al-dimā') through transgression. The angels contrasted these with their own continuous glorification and sanctification of Allah.

questions.question: According to Ibn Abbas (RA), what was the full scope of the knowledge in al-asmā' kullahā that Allah taught Adam?
options: The names of the angels ranked in their celestial orders
The 99 Names of Allah and the names of the prophets
The names of every single thing that exists — every creature, animal, object, and utensil
The names of all plants and heavenly bodies
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas (RA) explained that al-asmā' kullahā means Allah taught Adam the name of every single thing that exists, down to ordinary items like a bowl and ladle. This explains the ongoing expansion of human knowledge across science and technology.

questions.question: What does *tabkit* mean, and why is it the correct label for the spirit behind Allah's test of the angels?
options: A neutral examination designed to assess knowledge impartially
A reward-based test designed to confirm the angels' superiority
Encouragement, prompting the angels to recall what they knew
Rebuking and scolding — the angels had questioned humanity's fitness for khilafah, so the test was a direct challenge to that claim
questions.explanation: Tabkit means rebuking and scolding. The test was framed as a rebuke because the angels had raised objections to humanity's fitness for khilafah — by challenging them to name what they could not, Allah implicitly replied to their objection.

questions.question: What grammatical function does *Subḥān* serve in سُبْحَانَكَ as it appears in the angels' statement in Ayat 32?
options: Fā'il (subject) of an implied preceding verb
Mubtadā' (subject) in a nominal sentence, with *ka* as the khabar
Maf'ūl Mutlaq (cognate accusative/absolute object), with the verb and Fā'il implied before it
Maf'ūl Bihi (direct object) of an explicit preceding verb
questions.explanation: Subḥān is manṣūb (accusative) and functions as a Maf'ūl Mutlaq. The full implied sentence is نُسَبِّحُ سُبْحَانَكَ — 'We glorify You with glorification'; the verb and Fā'il are hidden, since the angels speak in the plural.

questions.question: What theological conclusion does the Qur'an's consistent use of the dual pronoun (*huma*) in Ayat 36 establish?
options: That Adam bore sole responsibility for the sin
That both Adam and Hawa were equally responsible for eating from the forbidden tree
That neither Adam nor Hawa was truly culpable for the act
That Hawa bore greater responsibility for the sin than Adam
questions.explanation: The dual form establishes that both Adam and Hawa were equally responsible — the sin cannot be attributed to Hawa alone. Surah Ṭā-Hā (20:121) reinforces this explicitly: *wa 'aṣā Ādamu rabbahu fa-ghawā*.

questions.question: What does *taba 'alā* indicate in Ayat 37, and to whom alone is it attributed?
options: The servant's act of turning back in repentance — it applies to any repentant person
A verbal noun describing the general state of sincere remorse
Allah's act of accepting repentance — attributed only to Allah
A shared act of turning between the servant and Allah at the moment of acceptance
questions.explanation: *Taba 'alā* is Allah's act of accepting repentance and is attributed only to Allah. Ayat 37 uses *fataba 'alayhi*, indicating that Allah accepted Adam's repentance. *Taba ilā* by contrast is the servant's act of turning back toward Allah.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the two interpretations of خَلِيفَة given in the tafseer of Ayat 30?
options: A title given exclusively to the prophets and messengers
A ruler chosen from among the angels to govern the earth
Adam (AS) specifically as the first vicegerent on earth
All humans collectively as a group responsible for communal worship
questions.explanation: One interpretation is Adam (AS) specifically as the first vicegerent on earth. The second is all of humanity as a continuous succession of generations, each succeeding the last and implementing Allah's rulings century after century.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between سُجُودُ تَحِيَّةٍ and sujudu 'ibadah?
options: Sujudu taḥiyyah requires full ritual purity; sujudu 'ibadah does not
Sujudu taḥiyyah is abrogated in Islamic law; sujudu 'ibadah remains in force
Sujudu taḥiyyah is prostration of greeting and respect; sujudu 'ibadah is worship prostration, permissible for Allah alone
Sujudu taḥiyyah is performed facing Makkah; sujudu 'ibadah may face any direction
questions.explanation: Sujudu taḥiyyah is prostration of greeting and respect, as the angels performed to Adam. Sujudu 'ibadah is prostration of worship, which is permissible for Allah alone — no created being may receive it.

questions.question: What does تَبْكِيت mean?
options: To inform and instruct
To praise and affirm
To rebuke and scold
To test neutrally and objectively
questions.explanation: Tabkit means rebuking and scolding. It is the correct label for the spirit in which Allah tested the angels who had questioned humanity's fitness for khilafah.

questions.question: What specific words did Adam receive through تَلَقَّى from his Lord?
options: The names of all created things
The words of the adhān and the opening adhkār
The opening words of Surah Al-Fātiḥah
The du'ā of Surah Al-A'raf 7:23: رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنفُسَنَا...
questions.explanation: تَلَقَّى means to receive. The mufassirun identify the words Adam received as the du'ā in Surah Al-A'raf 7:23: *Rabbanā ẓalamnā anfusanā wa in lam taghfir lanā wa tarḥamnā la-nakūnanna minal-khāsirīn*.

questions.question: What grammatical form is تَوَّاب built on, and what does that form convey about its meaning?
options: Ism al-Tafdīl (elative form), indicating Allah is the highest accepter of repentance
Ism al-Fā'il (active participle), indicating one who repents regularly
Ism al-Maf'ūl (passive participle), indicating one who is repeatedly forgiven
Ism al-Mubālaghah (fa''āl pattern), indicating Allah is extremely and abundantly accepting of repentance
questions.explanation: تَوَّاب is built on the Ism al-Mubālaghah pattern (fa''āl), denoting an intensive/superlative degree: Allah is extremely and abundantly accepting of repentance — kathīru al-qabūl lit-tawbah.

questions.question: What was the direct consequence of Iblis's act of اسْتَكْبَرَ?
options: He became minal kāfirīn — among the disbelievers
He was deprived of his ability to address the angels
He was stripped of his knowledge of the unseen
He was permanently expelled from all proximity to divine mercy
questions.explanation: اسْتَكْبَرَ means to become arrogant or haughty. The direct consequence of Iblis's arrogance was that he became minal kāfirīn — among the disbelievers.

questions.question: What does مَتَاع mean in the context of *mata'un ilā ḥīn* (Ayat 36)?
options: Temporary enjoyment or benefit, lasting only until one's appointed term
A severe trial that must be patiently endured
Eternal reward awaiting the righteous
A punishment that mirrors the enjoyment taken in disobedience
questions.explanation: مَتَاع means temporary enjoyment or benefit. In *mata'un ilā ḥīn*, it indicates that the pleasures of worldly life last only until one's appointed term — the world is not a permanent home.

questions.question: What grammatical category is أَلَا, and does it carry a position in *tarkīb*?
options: Harf nafy (particle of negation); it negates what follows and has no tarkīb position
Harf tanbi' (particle of alert/notice); it has no position in tarkīb
Harf shart (conditional particle); it has a position in tarkīb
Harf nidā' (particle of address); it occupies the position of the addressed noun
questions.explanation: أَلَا is a harf tanbi' (particle of alert/notice), drawing attention to what follows. It has no position in tarkīb — it carries no i'rāb role in the sentence structure.

questions.question: A woman bleeds for 4 days, has a 10-day clean gap, then bleeds for 3 more days. How is the entire period classified?
options: The first 4 days are Haid; the 10-day gap and final 3 days are Istihadah
One continuous Haid, because the clean gap is less than the minimum 15-day Tuhar
The 4 and 3-day bleedings are separate Haid; the 10-day gap qualifies as Tuhar
Two separate Haid episodes with a valid Tuhar between them
questions.explanation: The entire period counts as one continuous Haid because the clean gap between the two bleedings is less than 15 days. The minimum valid Tuhar separating two distinct Haid episodes is 15 days.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT permitted for a woman in Haid?
options: Reciting the Qur'an, whether from memory, a written copy, or by teaching recitation
Making du'ā using Qur'anic phrases with the intention of supplication
Listening to someone else recite the Qur'an aloud
Using non-verbal gestures to correct a student's recitation mistake
questions.explanation: A woman in Haid may not recite the Qur'an — from memory, a written copy, or by teaching recitation. She may make du'ā using Qur'anic phrases (with the intention of du'ā) and use non-verbal gestures to correct recitation.

questions.question: A leather belt is purchased from a store where the animal was almost certainly not slaughtered Islamically. What is the correct ruling?
options: It is Najis and impermissible to use or wear
It is Makrūh (disliked) but permissible for Salah
Proof of Islamic slaughter must be obtained before the hide can be used
It is pure; tanning purifies any animal hide regardless of how the animal was killed, with exceptions only for swine and humans
questions.explanation: Tanning (dabāghat) purifies any animal hide regardless of how the animal was killed — Zabiha is not a condition. The only two exceptions where tanning does not purify are the hides of swine (pigs) and humans.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the three conditions required for valid Masa over fabric socks (Jorabayn) according to the Muftabih opinion?
options: The sock must be water-resistant — wet hands pressed against it should not cause seepage within approximately 2–3 seconds
The socks must be made of natural fiber (wool or cotton)
Masa is only valid if both feet are covered with socks of identical material
The socks must be worn during a state of Wudu that has not broken since being put on
questions.explanation: One of the three conditions is that the sock must be water-resistant — wet hands pressed against it should not cause water to seep through within approximately 2–3 seconds. The other conditions are reaching above the ankle bone and being durable enough to walk approximately one mile.

questions.question: A person prays with a bloodstain larger than a dirham, discovered only after the prayer is complete. Is the prayer valid?
options: No — any Najasat above the pardoned threshold automatically invalidates the prayer
Yes — but only if the prayer was an obligatory (Fard) prayer, not a Nafl
Yes — the prayer is valid because the person was completely unaware while praying
No — they must repeat only the rak'ah during which the Najasat was likely present
questions.explanation: The prayer is valid and need not be repeated because the person was completely unaware while praying. Had they known about the stain exceeding the threshold before praying, the prayer would not have been permissible.

questions.question: What does Madhi (pre-seminal fluid) require in terms of purification, and how does this differ from Mani?
options: Madhi requires Wudu only; Mani requires full Ghusl
Both Madhi and Mani require Wudu only — no Ghusl
Madhi requires Ghusl, just like Mani
Madhi requires neither Ghusl nor Wudu; Mani requires Wudu only
questions.explanation: Madhi requires Wudu only — no Ghusl. This differs from Mani (semen), which requires full Ghusl. The dalil is the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), who reported that the Prophet ﷺ said Ghusl is not required for Madhi — only washing the area and making Wudu.

questions.question: What is the minimum duration of طُهر, and what does falling short of it mean for two episodes of bleeding?
options: 3 days — matching the minimum valid duration of Haid itself
10 days — any gap shorter means the bleeding continues as the same Haid
7 days — the typical duration between menstrual cycles
15 days — any gap shorter means both bleedings together count as one Haid
questions.explanation: The minimum Tuhar is 15 days. Any gap shorter than 15 days between two bleedings means the entire period — both bleedings plus the gap — counts as a single Haid, not two separate episodes.

questions.question: Which two animals' hides does دَبَاغَة (tanning) NOT purify?
options: Dogs and cats
Dogs and donkeys
Pigs and humans
Donkeys and pigs
questions.explanation: Tanning purifies any animal hide regardless of how the animal was killed. The only two exceptions are the hides of pigs (swine) and humans — tanning does not purify these.

questions.question: In Wudu, what does مَسْح refer to, and over what items can it be performed as an alternative to washing?
options: Washing; it is performed on the same limbs as regular Wudu
Pouring water; it is performed over the head and ears only
Drying; it follows washing the feet to complete the Wudu
Wiping; it can be performed over leather khuffain or fabric Jorabayn
questions.explanation: In Wudu, مَسْح refers to wiping — specifically wiping over footwear (leather khuffain or fabric Jorabayn) as a valid alternative to washing the feet, subject to its own conditions.

questions.question: What is the threshold of نَجَاسَت مُغَلَّظَة below which Salah remains valid (with Makruh Tanzihi dislike)?
options: Dirham size for liquid / 3.5 Masha (~3.2–3.5 g) for solid
Half a dirham for liquid Najasat
Any trace amount below half a gram is automatically pardoned
One-fourth of the garment for any type of Najasat
questions.explanation: Salah remains valid (with Makruh Tanzihi dislike) when the نَجَاسَت مُغَلَّظَة is below dirham size for liquid or below 3.5 Masha (~3.2–3.5 g) for solid. Above these thresholds, Salah is not permissible.

questions.question: At what threshold does نَجَاسَت مُخَفَّفَة render Salah impermissible?
options: Any visible trace on the garment
One-fourth (¼) or more of the garment
More than dirham size of the impurity
More than half the garment
questions.explanation: For نَجَاسَت مُخَفَّفَة (e.g., urine of Halal animals), Salah becomes impermissible at one-fourth (¼) or more of the garment. Below that threshold, Salah is valid with dislike.

questions.question: What does وَدِي require for purification?
options: Full Ghusl, as it exits with similar force to Mani
Wudu only — wash the area and make a fresh Wudu
Neither Ghusl nor Wudu; it is treated as a minor impurity
Both Ghusl and a fresh Wudu
questions.explanation: وَدِي is a thick discharge that sometimes appears after urination. It requires Wudu only — no Ghusl. The area should be washed and a fresh Wudu made.

questions.question: What relaxed rule applies to a مَرِيض with chronic, uncontrollable impurity in Tahara rulings?
options: They are permanently exempted from all purification obligations
They are exempt from Salah but must perform Tasbeeh as a substitute
They make one fresh Wudu per Salah time and may perform acts of worship within that time regardless of ongoing discharge
They must perform Ghusl before every Fard Salah
questions.explanation: A chronically ill person with uncontrollable, continuous impurity makes one fresh Wudu per Salah time and may perform Salah and any acts of worship within that time period, regardless of ongoing discharge during it.

questions.question: Does a person who prays while completely unaware of Najasat-e-Mughalaza above the pardoned threshold need to make قَضَاء?
options: No — the prayer is valid; Qadā is required only if they knowingly prayed with Najasat above the pardoned amount
Yes — but only if the Najasat was on the clothing rather than the body
Yes — any Najasat above the threshold requires Qadā regardless of the person's awareness
No — but they must recite Istighfār and repeat the final sajdah of that prayer
questions.explanation: No Qadā is required when the person was completely unaware while praying. Qadā would be required only if they knowingly prayed with Najasat-e-Mughalaza above the pardoned threshold.
